question: An angle is measured as $45^\circ$ with a possible error of $0.5^\circ$. Using linear approximation and differentials, estimate $\tan 45.5^\circ$, and hence determine the maximum approximate error and percentage error in the value of the tangent calculated from the measured angle.
explanation:
Conversion of Error
The measured angle is
$$\theta=45^\circ=\frac{\pi}{4}$$
The possible angular error in radians is
$$d\theta=0.5^\circ=\frac{\pi}{360}$$

Linear Approximation
Let $f(\theta)=\tan\theta$. Then
$$f'(\theta)=\sec^2\theta$$
At $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$,
$$f\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=1$$
and
$$f'\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=2$$
Therefore,
$$\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\pi}{360}\right)\approx 1+2\left(\frac{\pi}{360}\right)$$
$$\tan 45.5^\circ\approx 1+\frac{\pi}{180}\approx 1.01745$$

Error Estimation
The differential is
$$dy=\sec^2\theta\,d\theta$$
Hence, the maximum approximate error is
$$|dy|=2\left(\frac{\pi}{360}\right)=\frac{\pi}{180}\approx 0.01745$$
The corresponding percentage error is
$$\frac{|dy|}{|y|}\times 100=\frac{\pi}{180}\times 100$$
$$\approx 1.745\%$$
